We need a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

From earlier apply_template gave disconnection into two fragments: "COc1cccc(N)c1" (anisidine) and "Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1Cc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1". Actually product of template 647549 gave two fragments: first is COc1cccc(N)c1 (an aniline with methoxy). second is Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1Cc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1 (a triazine with carboxylic acid and side chain). So step1: disconnection of amide bond (amide formation forward). So retrosynthesis: target -> amide cleavage gives aniline and acid (or amine). So we have fragment A: anisidine (COc1cccc(N)c1). Fragment B: Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1Cc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1 (a triazine with carboxylic acid). Next we need to further disconnect fragment B. It contains a carboxylic acid attached to triazine ring (C(=O)O). Could be derived from amide formation? Actually we already broke amide; the remaining fragment B still has a carboxylic acid attached to triazine carbon (maybe from amide formation originally). Could be formed via amide coupling of amine on triazine? Wait B has "Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1..." The triazine ring has an exocyclic amine (N attached to carbonyl? Actually "Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1" indicates an aniline? The N attached to carbon of triazine? The pattern: N attached to aromatic carbon of triazine (position). So we could break that N-C bond via SN2? The N is primary amine attached to aromatic carbon (aryl amine). Could be formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) of a halide (e.g., aryl chloride) with amine. So step2: disconnection of that N-C bond, giving aryl halide (e.g., Clc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1) and amine (NH2). So we need a template for SN2? Actually SNAr is not SN2 but similar. But we have template for substitution of halogen with amine. Let's search for template where functional group broken is "aryl halide" and formed "primary amines".
